sources.title: AFI Catalog: The African Queen (1951)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected cast, literary source, synopsis and production note.
supports: Katharine Hepburn is credited as Rose Sayer.
The film is based on C. S. Forester's 1935 novel.
AFI's synopsis has Rose devise the plan against the German steamer Louisa, and its production history reports raft reproductions for boat close-ups.
limits: Rose and the plot are fictional narrative, not a documented account of one historical voyage or attack.
The setting is evidence for film context, not proof of every real historical detail in East Africa during 1914.

sources.organisation: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: Academy: The 24th Academy Awards (1952)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected ceremony release-year statement and African Queen award categories.
supports: The ceremony honors films released in 1951.
Humphrey Bogart won Actor for The African Queen, while Katharine Hepburn was an Actress nominee.
John Huston was nominated for Directing and James Agee with Huston for Screenplay.
limits: The ceremony page does not make Hepburn the Actress winner for this film.
It is an awards ledger, not a source for plot or character biography.

source_link.supports: Подтверждает победу Богарта, номинацию Хепбёрн и номинации Хьюстона/Эйджи за фильм 1951 года.

sources.title: AFI Catalog: Sunset Blvd. (1950)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected cast, narration, preview revision, self-referential silent-era material and credits.
supports: Gloria Swanson is credited as Norma Desmond.
The film begins with Joe Gillis narrating after his death, then flashes back; its original morgue opening was cut after preview audiences laughed.
AFI documents use of Queen Kelly footage and silent-era figures including von Stroheim, DeMille and Keaton.
limits: Norma is fictional despite the film's real Hollywood people, footage and locations.
AFI's contemporary title-card note uses Sunset Blvd.; title variation is not a separate film.

sources.organisation: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: Academy: The 23rd Academy Awards (1951)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected ceremony release-year statement and Sunset Blvd. results.
supports: The ceremony honors films released in 1950.
Gloria Swanson was an Actress nominee for Sunset Blvd.
Sunset Blvd. had eleven nominations and three wins: black-and-white art direction, Franz Waxman's score, and original story/screenplay by Brackett, Wilder and Marshman.
limits: The page lists a nomination, not an Actress win, for Swanson.
It is an awards ledger and does not establish the character credit; AFI supplies that credit.
